e-7196.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Non-Partitioned Region
e-7196.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
$\displaystyle \int_0^1 \int_{y^3}^{1} f(x,y) \: \textrm{d}x \: \textrm{d}y.$
e-7196.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/47b8a129674d4644593741607e0efd5dea1ffde45357f327e3af4e08d0bf423d.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D= \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq1, \quad y^3 \leq x \leq 1 \big\},
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x = y^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y = \sqrt[3]{x},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y = 0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D= \big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 0 \leq y \leq \sqrt[3]{x} \big\}.
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e627a8750d3f5055b3936d47100fc51ae68926dfdc0c53d020638c9ef99f9b27.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7195.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Partitioned Region
e-7195.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral $\displaystyle \int_0^1\int_{2x}^{3-x} f(x,y)\,\textrm{d}y\,\textrm{d}x .$
e-7195.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/47f6b583b2dd059ad8df49b0ca4374a964b4a28e91eb242a0dd3c7b8476fd26e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \quad 2x \leq y \leq 3-x \big\}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/35b4b57f26c7903189899ec284faa39bb70fb3a80397b772376358d4d86b3ec1.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$$
x=\dfrac{y}{2}.
$$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=3-y.
$$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
D_1 = \Big\{ (x,y) \::\: 0 \leq y \leq 2, \quad 0 \leq x \leq \dfrac{y}{2} \Big\}
$$

and

$$
D_2 = \Big\{ (x,y) \::\: 2 \leq y \leq 3, \quad 0 \leq x \leq 3-y \Big\}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2x}^{3-x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/a65b8ea83edc85a0b0ec3f3df6ee6f5bc841e9cb5d634aab963054f836965146.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le {x}^{2}+1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{2}+1\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y-1},
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 5,\,\sqrt{y-1}\le x\le 2},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d10ba1db82f9d0366edb446f8bef564030fea2068066c7f05f388f0c9daa3414.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{\sqrt{y-1}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Change the order of integration in the double integral ∫02∫1x2+1f(x,y)dydx.

a
∫15∫y−12f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫15∫2y−1f(x,y)dxdy
c

d
∫04∫y+14f(x,y)dxdy

∫04∫y−12f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,1≤y≤x2+1}.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is y=x2+1⟹x=y−1, and the right boundary of the region is x=2.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is D={(x,y):1≤y≤5,y−1≤x≤2}, as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫02∫1x2+1f(x,y)dydx=∫15∫y−12f(x,y)dxdy.

content.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/a65b8ea83edc85a0b0ec3f3df6ee6f5bc841e9cb5d634aab963054f836965146.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le {x}^{2}+1}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{2}+1\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y-1},
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=2.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 5,\,\sqrt{y-1}\le x\le 2},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/d10ba1db82f9d0366edb446f8bef564030fea2068066c7f05f388f0c9daa3414.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{{x}^{2}+1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{\sqrt{y-1}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The region satisfies 1 ≤ x ≤ e and 0 ≤ y ≤ ln(x). Hence 0 ≤ y ≤ 1, and y ≤ ln(x) gives x ≥ e^y. The reversed bounds are e^y ≤ x ≤ e, so option e is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/def6c95bc51de3e02b913d9951cce283285cd8049375c6842719c46d33a29a15.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,⟹\,x={e}^{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=e.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le e},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e38a26dbfaa0c126ec31b44f2a7d31225666779bea7b6f8b67dc2cd04e703114.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

D={(x,y):1≤x≤e,0≤y≤ln⁡x}.

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

y=ln⁡x⟹x=ey

and the right boundary of the region is

x=e.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,ey≤x≤e},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫1e∫0ln⁡xf(x,y)dydx=∫01∫eyef(x,y)dxdy.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Non-Partitioned Region
content.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/def6c95bc51de3e02b913d9951cce283285cd8049375c6842719c46d33a29a15.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,⟹\,x={e}^{y}
$$

and the right boundary of the region is

$$
x=e.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le e},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/e38a26dbfaa0c126ec31b44f2a7d31225666779bea7b6f8b67dc2cd04e703114.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/8287ba53b227ddc36aff486ea8d42a83203940ee265163320c19ad6cdb39089e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}.
$$

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/2c9a41f06d7edfbad9756923d9b70f1d0ffd730350d0b7d2d0e109c1bca9f80d.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

c

EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤1,0≤y≤x2}.

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form y=y(x), is

y=x2⟹x=y

and the left boundary of the region is

x=0.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤y≤1,0≤x≤y},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫01∫x21f(x,y)dydx=∫01∫0yf(x,y)dxdy.

content.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
content.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/8287ba53b227ddc36aff486ea8d42a83203940ee265163320c19ad6cdb39089e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le {x}^{2}}.
$$

Notice that the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y={x}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{y}
$$

and the left boundary of the region is

$$
x=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type II region. The type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{y}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/2c9a41f06d7edfbad9756923d9b70f1d0ffd730350d0b7d2d0e109c1bca9f80d.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{5}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/7e0a0b1860f316f7954e85b9d7f6567d9e0c05bf316cb8af3901037abe6fd17e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡5,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le 5}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x={e}^{y}\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3c95dd90ad02ab708f5893e47e7d7d0c8a212c18aed1972fb1bba1362181c383.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{5}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b
∫1e∫ln⁡x2f(x,y)dydx
c
∫24∫1ln⁡xf(x,y)dydx
d
∫15∫0ln⁡xf(x,y)dydx
e
∫15∫1ln⁡xf(x,y)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is D={(x,y):0≤y≤ln⁡5,ey≤x≤5}.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is x=ey⟹y=ln⁡x, and the bottom boundary of the region is y=0.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is D={(x,y):1≤x≤5,0≤y≤ln⁡x},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫0ln⁡5∫ey5f(x,y)dxdy=∫15∫0ln⁡xf(x,y)dydx.

verification.explanation: Since e^y ≤ x is equivalent to y ≤ ln(x), the region becomes 1 ≤ x ≤ 5 and 0 ≤ y ≤ ln(x). The worked solution confirms option d; the deliberately incorrect submission selected c.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Non-Partitioned Region
content.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{5}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
content.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/7e0a0b1860f316f7954e85b9d7f6567d9e0c05bf316cb8af3901037abe6fd17e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡5,\,{e}^{y}\le x\le 5}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x={e}^{y}\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{ln}⁡x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/3c95dd90ad02ab708f5893e47e7d7d0c8a212c18aed1972fb1bba1362181c383.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{\int }_{{e}^{y}}^{5}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The region is 1 ≤ y ≤ 2 and 2y−2 ≤ x ≤ 2. Solving for y gives y ≤ (x+2)/2, so the reversed bounds are 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 and 1 ≤ y ≤ (x+2)/2. This is option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2y-2}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
after.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/062d32beb0cab13297c21b2eab703fd5e598191c96daa93a9c27337af95a1930.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,2y-2\le x\le 2}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=2y-2\,⟹\,y=\frac{x+2}{2},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le \frac{x+2}{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/543ffc57d0d32ae9a4bdefa87bd56deb7380061004b7737cf821117b4fb20e2f.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2y-2}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{(x+2)/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Change the order of integration in the double integral ∫12∫2y−22f(x,y)dxdy.

a
∫(x+2)/22∫01f(x,y)dydx
b
∫02∫1(x+2)/2f(x,y)dydx
c
∫01∫2(x+2)/2f(x,y)dydx
d
∫02∫(x+2)/21f(x,y)dydx
e
∫0(x+2)/2∫12f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

D={(x,y):1≤y≤2,2y−2≤x≤2}.

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form x=x(y), is

x=2y−2⟹y=x+22,

and the bottom boundary of the region is

y=1.

To change the order of integration, we write D as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,1≤y≤x+22},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

∫12∫2y−22f(x,y)dxdy=∫02∫1(x+2)/2f(x,y)dydx.

content.knowledge_point: Swapping the Order of Integration on a Non-Partitioned Region
content.problem: Change the order of integration in the double integral ${\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2y-2}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.$
content.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/062d32beb0cab13297c21b2eab703fd5e598191c96daa93a9c27337af95a1930.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. It is a type II region, and its type II representation is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,2y-2\le x\le 2}.
$$

Notice that the top boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$$
x=2y-2\,⟹\,y=\frac{x+2}{2},
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region is

$$
y=1.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as a type I region. The type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,1\le y\le \frac{x+2}{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071085/assets/543ffc57d0d32ae9a4bdefa87bd56deb7380061004b7737cf821117b4fb20e2f.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{2y-2}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{(x+2)/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
